# A ball from a two-limb center and a radius

Kernel `ball_make_2` · **UNVERIFIED** · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

**UNVERIFIED: no proof is checked.** The statement below is a target: Rocq has not checked a proof of it. An operation that calls this kernel compiles only with the marker `kairn::unverified` on an operand, and `kairn::traits` exports no constants for it ([What holds today](../getting-started/guarantees.md#proved-and-unverified)).

## What it computes

The ball of center $c$ and radius $r$, or the empty set or the whole line when they do not make a finite ball:

$$Z = \{\, t : \lvert t - c\rvert \le r \,\}.$$

A number of several limbs stands for their exact sum: $c = c_0 + c_1$, $c_w = c_{w0} + c_{w1}$.

## C++

| Form | Operands | Result | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Ball<T, 2>(c, r)` | `Expansion<T, 2>`, `T` | `Ball<T, 2>` |  |
| `Ball<T, 2>(c)` | `Expansion<T, 2>` | `Ball<T, 2>` | implicit: the point $c$, radius 0 |
| `Ball<T, 2>(a)` | `T` | `Ball<T, 2>` | implicit: the point $a$, radius 0, with the center made by `make_2` first |

`T` is `float` or `double`; the operations are in namespace `kairn`, header `kairn/kairn.hpp`. The operators and functions also accept the marker `kairn::unverified` on an operand, which they need while the kernel is UNVERIFIED (a constructor does not take it).

## Requires

- $c$ is canonical: finite and normalized, or $(\pm\infty, \pm 0)$, or $(\mathrm{NaN}, \mathrm{NaN})$.
- $r$ is any value of `T`: a number, $\pm\infty$ or a NaN.

## Target (not proved)

For operands that satisfy the requirements, finite, infinite or NaN:

- The result $Z$, of center $c_w$ and radius $r_w$, is a canonical ball.
- $Z$ is the empty set (every limb a NaN) when $r$ is negative, $-\infty$ included.
- Otherwise $Z$ is the whole line (center 0, radius $+\infty$) when $r$ is a NaN or $+\infty$, or $c$ is not finite.
- Otherwise $Z$ is the ball of center $c$ and radius $r$, exactly.

Stated for every binary format with a precision of at least 1 bit, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the IEEE model, with signed zeros, infinities, NaN and overflow. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**UNVERIFIED.** No proof of the statement is checked. The [Proofs](../proofs/index.md#what-is-proved-and-in-which-model) page says which statements of the IEEE model are proved against statements written by hand; this page gives the status that `gen/claims.json` gives.

## Source

**Algorithm:** constructors (Milestone 1 listing; a NaN radius the whole line, 2026-11-20). **License:** algorithm: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/ball_make_2.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/ball_make_2.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal model (`proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).

```
# A ball from a canonical 2-limb center (an object, so its limbs are stored) and a radius from the
# program, guarded (rule R3): the empty set when the radius is negative, -infinity included (n
# true); otherwise the whole line when the center is not finite or the radius is +infinity or a
# NaN (f false: lt(g, const inf) is false for a NaN), as a NaN bound given to an interval is (the
# owner's decision of 2026-11-20); and otherwise the ball itself (milestone1.md, "Values that enter
# from the program"). The ordinary case is the first arm of each select (ok = not(n)), as the
# scalar printer's branch over a fix-up wants. The IEEE-model proof (proofs/theories/IeeeMake.v)
# is of the rule before, that a NaN radius gives the empty set, and is being redone for this one:
# unverified until then.

g   = guard(r)
n   = lt(g, 0)
ok  = not(n)
a   = abs(c0)
f1  = lt(a, const inf)
f2  = lt(g, const inf)
f   = and(f1, f2)
k0  = select(f, c0, 0)
k1  = select(f, c1, 0)
s   = select(f, g, const inf)
cw0 = select(ok, k0, const nan)
cw1 = select(ok, k1, const nan)
rw  = select(ok, s, const nan)
```

## Measured

The latest brute-force runs, from the stored summaries in [`results/milestone1/brute/`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/tree/main/results/milestone1/brute) ([the report](../developer/results/brute-milestone1.md#ball_make_2)): the oracle judged, in exact arithmetic, the results of the compiled kernel (every compiler, scalar and packed code, every contraction setting) on random operands of `binary64` and `binary32`, and those of the generator's interpreter on every operand of small formats. A measurement, not a bound.
They judged the kernel in the extended domain, infinite and NaN operands included, as the oracle reads its statement in the IEEE model ([Claims of the non-finite layer](../developer/architecture.md#claims-of-the-non-finite-layer)).

| Run | Cases judged | Failed |
|---|---|---|
| `binary64` (`double`), compiled: 60 runners on 3 machines | 112 800 000 | 0 |
| `binary32` (`float`), compiled: 60 runners on 3 machines | 112 800 000 | 0 |
| toy formats, every operand: 6 domains of 6 formats | 11 490 416 | 0 |
| toy formats, every operand, supplementary run: 1 domain of 1 format | 896 | 0 |

## Not claimed

- Anything for operands that do not satisfy the requirements.
- The sign of a zero limb, and which NaN a NaN result is: the claims compare neither.
- Anything at all, as a guarantee: the statement is a target until its proof is checked.
